# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–4 (Complete and Final – Updated 59)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford; Also: Chiswick Mall (Miss Pinkerton's academy), Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn
- **Current Setting Details**: River crossing at Gulton and Quenwick; forge with chalked crooked sun on wall; wind from water with salt and tar smell; gulls quarreling over fish heads by steps; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; frost silvering hedges overnight; turnip cart passing well; light going early as spring approaches; children chasing hoop down lane; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; market town of Bryngate; hill farms of Coldcombe and Mirecombe; bees humming in lavender behind parsonage; bell for vespers ringing thinly across roofs; rain threatening but holding off; front room on second floor with chintz tent hung round with rich India pattern and double calico of tender rose-colour, featherbed with two pillows, two round red faces; back drawing-room with piano situated in darkness

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return to Middlemarch; now married with infant son
- **Family Reconciliation**: Initial opposition resolved; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea and Will's cousins enjoy playing with visiting children
- **Sir James's Opposition**: Never ceased regarding second marriage as mistake; tradition in Middlemarch that she married sickly clergyman then within year gave up estate to marry propertyless cousin
- **Dorothea's Life Assessment**: Acts not ideally beautiful but mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive; growing good of world partly dependent on unhistoric acts

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- **Present Status**: Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window
- **Marriage Achievement**: Solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations
- **Fred's Development**: Remains steady; told Mary happiness half owing to Farebrother; never wholly free from misled hopefulness but gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner
- **Fred's Feelings**: Had pleasant vision of bright hearth; told Mary magnanimously Farebrother was worthier; sorry for other men who could not have Mary
- **Children**: Three boys only; youngest resembles grandfather; minimal formal teaching but children found quite forward at school

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)**
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; dressed in white with bare shoulders
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist
- **Departure from Chiswick**: Said French farewell to Miss Pinkerton; threw Dixonary at Miss Jemima; sank back in easy frame of mind; nobody cried for her leaving
- **Character**: Had dismal precocity of poverty; showed no will rivaling Miss Pinkerton's; never had been a girl, was woman since age eight; determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed in life since age eight when caught stealing jam by godmother; capable of calculated charm and intimacy
- **Position Obtained**: Miss Pinkerton recommended her for governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family after months-long battle to cancel indentures; Miss Pinkerton stated "I cannot find fault with Miss Sharp's conduct except to myself; must allow her talents and accomplishments are of high order"; petition for extension of leave already despatched before winter; difficult to find pretext for abruptly dismissing her
- **Crisp Affair**: Reverend Mr. Crisp, fresh from Oxford and curate to Vicar Flowerdew of Chiswick, fell in love and proposed in intercepted note; **rumor claims** tart-woman hinted great deal more than public knowledge; Mrs. Crisp summoned him from Buxton; truth of his letter unknown
- **At Sedley Household**: Invited by friend Miss Sedley for week before governess duties; Amelia showed her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl brought from India by brother Joseph; won over entire household through charming behavior
- **Regarding Joseph Sedley**: Upon learning of India shawls, Rebecca determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"; redoubled caresses to Amelia; vowed never to part with white cornelian necklace
- **Meeting Joseph**: Went downstairs with arm round Amelia's waist; agitated at drawing-room door; dressed in white with bare shoulders as white as snow
- **At Dinner**: Thought she must be quiet about India; at chili, laid down fork crying "Water, for Heaven's sake, water!"; swallowed mortification, made comical good-humoured air about Arabian Nights, cream-tarts, and cayenne
- **Joseph's Panic**: During two or three days following dinner, Joseph did not visit house nor mention Miss Rebecca's name; Miss Rebecca was respectful to Mrs. Sedley, delighted at Bazaars, wheeled to theatre by Mrs. Sedley
- **Amelia's Support**: When Amelia had headache and could not attend pleasure party, Rebecca refused to go without her, saying "What! you who have shown the poor orphan what happiness and love are for the first time in her life--quit YOU? Never!"; green eyes filled with tears; Mrs. Sedley found her charming
- **Winning Over Household**: Laughed at Mr. Sedley's jokes with cordiality pleasing to that good-natured gentleman; interested Mrs. Blenkinsop in raspberry-jam preserving; called Sambo "Sir" and "Mr. Sambo" delighting him; apologized to lady's maid with sweetness and humility; charmed both Drawing Room and Servants' Hall
- **Familiarity with Family**: By day ten of stay, on footing of considerable familiarity with family; Amelia loved her like sister
- **Hand Pressure Incident**: Gave Joseph gentle pressure with little hand, drew it back frightened, looked in his face then down at carpet-rods; Joseph's heart thumped at involuntary, timid motion of regard
- **Joseph's Feelings Rekindled**: Joseph thought "I exactly begin to feel as I did at Dumdum with Miss Cutler"; made many sweet appeals to Rebecca about dinner dishes
- **Vauxhall Plan**: Amelia reminded Joseph of Easter promise to take her to Vauxhall, proposing Rebecca should go with them now; **actual outcome**: Thunderstorm on evening appointed for Vauxhall party prevented attendance; young people remained at home instead and declared themselves rather glad of storm than otherwise
- **Intimate Evening at Home**: Left alone with Joseph Sedley in drawing-room while Amelia and George Osborne went to piano in back drawing-room; Rebecca occupied in knitting green silk purse; conversation with Joseph established great confidence and intimacy; talk carried on in low, becoming tone

**Joseph Sedley**
- **Position and Background**: In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint and returned to Europe; does not live with family but has own lodgings like gay young bachelor
- **Appearance and Habits**: Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres, appears at opera; at home in morning costume of those days' dandy; extremely talkative in man's society
- **Initial Reaction to Rebecca**: Bounced off arm-chair at her appearance, blushed excessively, hid face in neckcloths, continued huge clattering at poker and tongs, said "For heaven's sake see if my buggy's at the door. I CAN'T wait. I must go"
- **Entertainment and Sleep**: Burst out laughing at Rebecca's chili incident; fell asleep during dinner story; tells Indian stories repeatedly
- **Indulgences After Dinner**: Contented himself with bottle of claret besides Madeira at dinner; ate couple plates of strawberries and cream and twenty-four little rout cakes; thought great deal about girl upstairs; noticed her drop handkerchief twice at dinner; drank fitting quantity of port-wine tete-a-tete with George Osborne in dining-room during thunderstorm evening
- **Cowardice**: Nearly cried with vexation at father's joke about ordering elephant from Exeter 'Change; father stopped joking and offered champagne saying "It's all fair on the Stock Exchange, Jos"
- **Escape to Theatre**: Slipped away on pointed toes of his boots to see Forty Thieves and Miss Decamp's dance without waking father
- **Prediction re Rebecca**: Destined to be prey to woman as father goes on 'Change daily; first woman who fishes for him will hook him
- **Thunderstorm Evening**: Left tete-a-tete with Rebecca at drawing-room table; cast eyes down towards favourite Hessian boots; heaved something very like sigh

**Miss Amelia Sedley**
- **Character**: Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; friends with Miss Sharp; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister after ten days; has natural infirmity of tears, described as defect of "silly little thing"
- **Family Connections**: Brother Joseph (collector); godson George Osborne (family friend for twenty-three years); parents Mr. and Mrs. Sedley
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; fell in love or appeared to fall in love with George Osborne at single instant when he asked her for music; went with him to piano in back drawing-room; put hand into his in darkness, ostensibly so he could guide her among chairs and ottomans
- **Possessions**: White cornelian necklace, Cashmere shawls, sprigged muslin, embroidered beautiful pair of braces for brother Joseph; wrote note to George Osborne on Twelfth-night previously (misspelled "twelfth" without the "f")

**George Osborne**
- **Background and Family Connection**: Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; received silver cup at six weeks old from John Sedley; received coral with gold whistle and bells at six months; regularly "tipped" at Christmas by old gentleman; thrashed by Joseph Sedley when latter was hobbadyhoy and George was impudent urchin of ten years old; as familiar with family as daily acts of kindness and intercourse could make him
- **Character and Feelings**: Clever artist; at comfortable evening during thunderstorm, did not seem least disappointed at Vauxhall cancellation; felt extraordinary, almost irresistible impulse to seize Amelia in arms and kiss her in face of company
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying Amelia; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with Amelia at single instant; went with her to piano in back drawing-room during thunderstorm evening; allowed her to put hand in his for guidance

**Mr. Sedley**: Amelia and Joseph's father; coarse man from Stock Exchange; jocular, good-natured gentleman; made joke about Joseph and elephant; defended Joseph's vanity in curtain lecture conversation with wife; predicted Joseph destined to be prey to woman; "it's a mercy he did not bring us over a black daughter-in-law"

**Mrs. Sedley**: Good-natured lady; took Rebecca to Bazaars and theatre; initially felt maternal jealousy regarding Miss Sharp but could not suppose humble governess would dare look up to Collector of Boggley Wollah; by morning after Vauxhall plan, no longer thought of executing threats to dismiss Rebecca; conducted curtain lecture with husband in tent-like bedroom hung with India pattern chintz and rose-colour calico; took husband to task for cruel conduct to poor Joe

## Secondary and Minor Characters
**Miss Jemima**: Pulled Miss Sharp away after Dixonary incident; embraced Miss Sedley; almost fainted with terror

**Miss Pinkerton**: Proprietor of Chiswick Mall academy; large Roman-nosed, tall as grenadier; does not understand French; waved hand by way of adieu; tossed turban indignantly; called Minerva in narrative

**Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Housekeeper; interested in raspberry-jam preserving

**Sambo**: Servant delighted to be called "Sir" and "Mr. Sambo" by Rebecca

**Dr. Gollop**: Joseph's apothecary; Joseph tells him Artillery ball story repeatedly

**Reverend Mr. Crisp**: Fresh from Oxford; curate to Vicar Flowerdew; fell in love with Rebecca; proposed in intercepted note; carried off by mother from Buxton

**Alderman Balls**: Hosted dinner at Highbury Barn to which elders of Sedley house were invited on thunderstorm evening

**Multiple Named Individuals**: Stenworth, Lindson, Hollwood, Orlwood, Wexwood, Corrett, Hollett families; Conar Hollett and Jolia Hollett complained of aching backs; Madan and Dadette commented on salt prices; Feten and Jolia Hollett discussed weather, harvest, lame horse; Conar and Islan Lindner discussed weather, harvest, lame horse; Dadette predicted rain wrongly; Ilena mended torn sleeve by window; Wevie walked long way round to avoid muddy square; Madrek counted coins twice, came up penny short

## Rumors and Unverified Claims Preserved
- Wife of Ridan Corrett confided to Ilzek Wexwood that bridge toll at Salwick skimmed every month
- Gossip claimed Thidrek Corrett and Rira Stenworth wed in secret
- Tart-woman hinted great deal more than public knowledge regarding Mr. Crisp and Miss Sharp; his letter truth unknown
- Lindson blood debt to Hollmere; Lindson mill ledger rewritten after flood; Salford granary fire set on purpose; old abbey at Salford second cellar; Bryngate pastures deed forged; silver chest buried beneath Mirecombe well; Quenwick chapel vault opens only for living person with jade ring and oak comb; Dunholt toll bridge belonged to Wexwood family
